title: Esmeralda catalog
description: Shape of the Esmeralda catalog: every source document (catalog/ files or any other source adapter) and the resolved catalog that `esmeralda catalog resolve` produces. Each document carries `schema: esmeralda.catalog` and an integer `schema_version`. Changes are additive only; only a breaking change bumps `schema_version`.

dimension_name.description: Usage-event dimension key (snake_case, like the usage-event fields).

gateway.description: Gateway role or product for a hop: direct is the always-available floor.

projects.description: Attribution only: aliases of the projects this team owns (infra-cost chargeback). A project_labels source may fill it for a team declared in catalog files; it never creates teams or cost centres.

team_profile.description: Team-owned metadata (teams/<team>/team.yaml); the team itself is registered in teams.yaml.

example.description: Illustrative entry: resolved and shown, but never compiled into enforcement unless a non-example target references it.

identity.description: Verified identity of a caller. Values come from unit outputs (`ref: <unit>:<output>`) whenever the platform creates the identity; literal ids only for identities owned elsewhere.

caller.description: A non-workload identity (VM, human group, partner app, other-cloud workload) mapped to the team that pays for its calls. Workload callers (agents) are targets and need no entry here.

agent_gateway.description: false: this caller reaches its targets directly (for example an Apigee proxy runtime), never through the Agent Gateway. It still gets the target's IAM (run.invoker / aiplatform.user) but is left out of the per-target roles/iap.egressor lists (iap_egress).

target_caller.description: What one caller may do on a target, and how its calls are billed.

product.description: Apigee API product granting this caller access

cost_centers.description: Declared cost centres this caller may bill to (subset of its team's)

unit.description: layer-5-workloads unit that deploys the target

oneOf.description: A target Esmeralda does not deploy (brownfield API, agent on another cloud, external gateway). Non-example ones get their own Agent Registry entry (http and non-Google model: endpoint; mcp: MCP server; a2a: agent card) and a per-target roles/iap.egressor list compiled from callers; Google API hosts (*.googleapis.com) are layer-4 Google API entries instead, reachable only by the agents that declare the API in google_apis.

endpoint.description: Exact https URL. Environment-specific parts are placeholders the registering unit substitutes from layer outputs: {domain} (the entry point domain, as <label>.{domain}) and {region}.

token.description: id: Google ID token (Cloud Run IAM); access: OAuth2 access token (Agent Runtime)

target.description: An agent, MCP server, model or legacy API that callers reach through a gateway. Closed through target_strict / target_document (unevaluatedProperties).

description.description: Why the target exists, in one or two sentences. Required for targets with an Agent Registry entry (deployed MCP servers and agents, managed: false targets): it becomes the entry's description, followed by a generated "Used by: <callers>".

identity.description: Identity this target calls out as, when it is itself a caller

google_apis.description: Agents (a2a, adk) only: the Google APIs this agent calls through the Agent Gateway, beyond policy.agent_gateway.google_apis.baseline. Compiled into its own roles/iap.egressor grant on each API's Agent Registry entry; an API no agent declares is not registered, so the gateway denies it.

system.description: Descriptive grouping (for example a Backstage System); never used for enforcement.

runtime.description: Where the target runs. Inventory data: an external source may fill it on a target adopted through deploy.registry.

runtime_resource.description: Full resource name of the runtime resource, with placeholders for environment-specific ids.

source_pin.description: Adoption pin: this catalog file entry adopts the entry with registry.id == id that the external source `source` (a name in sources.yaml) reports. External entries never match a catalog entry by name.

registry_data.description: What an external source reports about an entry (inventory data, informational).

id.description: Stable id of the entry in its source; adoption pins match on it.

skills.description: Informational (A2A card skills); never a tools grant.

inventory_entry.description: Something an external source discovered that no catalog file adopts. Resolved and shown, never compiled: no IAM, no Agent Gateway policy, no registry write, no allowlist. Carries inventory and attribution data only.

google_apis.description: Google APIs by catalog name (aiplatform, aiplatform_runtime_region, bigquery, bigquerystorage, storage, telemetry, ...). The resolver accepts only the APIs of its known-hosts table (esmeralda.catalog.GOOGLE_APIS): real, serving hostnames, no mTLS / multi-region / REP variants.

unmapped_caller.description: An authenticated caller that is not in the catalog: deny (403, fail closed) or flag (allow, mark the record unattributed and alert). flag is accepted only in the environments listed in flag_environments, and never widens a gateway or IAM grant.

declared_mismatch.description: A declared cost centre the catalog does not allow for the verified caller: reject (403) or bill_own_team (bill the caller's verified team and flag the record).

flag_environments.description: Environments where unmapped_caller: flag (and label_mismatch: warn) is accepted (default: [dev]).

label_mismatch.description: Resolve-time: inventory or attribution metadata from an external source (project labels, ...) disagrees with the catalog files: fail (default) or warn. warn is accepted only in flag_environments. Separate from declared_mismatch, which is a per-request runtime rule.

agent_gateway.description: How the Agent Gateway roles/iap.egressor lists are compiled: per-target lists from target callers, Google API entries from google_apis.

google_apis.description: Google APIs every agent runtime may reach (granted to the agent projects, so a replaced engine can start before its new identity is granted). Agents add their own in google_apis.

shared_workload_identity.description: Identity every agent caller also uses (shared invoker service account while native Agent Identity auth is off), listed on targets of these kinds that have at least one agent caller.

collection_document.description: A file holding maps of teams, callers, targets and/or the policy (teams.yaml, policy.yaml, callers.yaml, external/*).

paths.description: files: paths relative to the catalog directory

options.description: Source-type options. Snapshot sources: snapshot (path under catalog/, default snapshots/{source}/{env}.json), optional (a missing snapshot is a warning while no catalog file adopts one of the source's entries), fields (narrow the source's capabilities).

sources_document.description: catalog/sources.yaml: which sources the resolver merges, in order.

environment_document.description: catalog/environments/<env>.yaml: overrides only, deep-merged last (maps merge, lists replace, null deletes).

sources.description: The merged sources, in order, then the environment overrides file: a name, or {name, type, snapshot, sha256} for a source read from a snapshot (sha256 of the snapshot file, null when an optional source has none).

inventory.description: Discovered entries (external, not adopted by a catalog file): never compiled.

provenance.description: Where each value came from: '<section>.<name>' for every entry, '<section>.<name>.<field path>' for fields an external source contributed, a shadowed loser, or an environment override.
